title: Exposure and composition in photography
subtitle: A small complete teaching package for the extension acceptance test.
summary: Original educational examples using fictional scenes. This non-production fixture tests a second topic without app changes.

refreshers.title: What you need
refreshers.markdown: A camera is optional. Compare the written scenes and make a reasoned choice.

modules.summary: Separate motion, light, and rendered brightness.
objectives: Explain the effect and limitation of a deliberate choice.

objectives: Explain the effect and limitation of a deliberate choice.

claims.description: Original educational photography guidance, with fictional scenes. These examples are test content, not a manufacturer specification.
claims.context: General principles and deliberately bounded creative judgments.

concepts.definition: A shorter exposure time reduces the distance a moving subject travels during exposure, reducing motion blur. It also captures less light under otherwise identical conditions.
Exposure concerns light reaching the sensor over time. Display brightness also depends on signal gain and rendering. Raising ISO does not itself admit more light through the lens.
Composition is an intentional arrangement of attention. Subject placement, contrast, scale, and surrounding space can each change what the viewer notices first.
The edge of a photograph decides what context is included and what is cut off. Inspect all four edges before capture, especially bright intrusions and awkward partial objects.

scenarios.title: Explain a cyclist photograph
scenarios.context: An original fictional scene for a content-only extension test. No camera execution is claimed.
scenarios.task: Propose two ways to show the cyclist’s motion and explain the capture tradeoff.
requirements: Explain a meaningful alternative and how you would compare the result.
scenarios.model: Use a short exposure to emphasize a sharp cyclist or a longer exposure to show movement. At the same aperture and scene light the shorter duration gathers less light. Check motion and brightness separately, and do not claim a tripod freezes the subject.
scenarios.reasoning: The response connects a choice to an intention, preserves a defensible alternative, and names evidence to inspect instead of grading by a rigid rule.

scenarios.title: Choose a café portrait frame
scenarios.context: An original fictional scene for a content-only extension test. No camera execution is claimed.
scenarios.task: Propose two portrait frames that balance the person and café context.
requirements: Explain a meaningful alternative and how you would compare the result.
scenarios.model: Compare a tighter frame that emphasizes expression with a wider frame that includes the café deliberately. Inspect the bright menu at the edge; either include it as useful context or change viewpoint so it stops competing. Explain why the chosen version better fits the story.
scenarios.reasoning: The response connects a choice to an intention, preserves a defensible alternative, and names evidence to inspect instead of grading by a rigid rule.
